The epitope specific E111 neutralized DENV1 16007 (genotype 2). E111 potently neutralized DENV1 genotypes 2 and 5, and poorly neutralized genotypes 1, 3 and 4. MAb E111 effectively neutralized DENV1 16007 when premixed with the virus before cell attachment or when added after virus attachment to the cell surface. The EC50 values for neutralization were similar at 37ºC or 40ºC over a period of 4.5 h, and only decreased after 22 h suggesting E111 epitopes become exposed for binding with time.

The epitope residues recognized by Mab MA28-7 were deduced based on the ability to neutralize different strains of enterovirus 71 (EV71) in a standard micro-neutralization assay using Vero cells. Mab MA28-7 neutralized EV71 strains C7/Osaka (genotype B4), SK-EV006 (genotype B3) and 1095/Shiga (genotype C2). It did not neutralize EV71 strains Nagoya (genotype B1), Bulgaria (genotype B1) or BrCr/tr (genotype A). Within the MA28-7-binding footprint VP1, only the epitope residues, especially Gly-145, were conserved among the neutralization-sensitive strains.

Epitope residues on  polio virus type 1 critical for neutralization activity of VHH PVSP19B were determined by selection of viral escape mutants. Poliovirus type 1 Mahoney was treated with the VHH and used to infect HeLa cells. Mutants with amino acid substitutions A43T (VP1)/E168G (VP1), A43T (VP1)/E168K (VP1), or V166L (VP1)/A222V (VP1) escaped neutralization with the VHH. Substitutions A43T in VP1 was located far from the binding site on the inner surface of the virion and may act by a mechanism other than steric interference with antibody binding.

The epitope-specific VHH PVSP29F neutralized infection by polio virus type 1. VHH PVSP29F was shown to interfere with an early phase of viral replication by adding the VHH at various stages of the infection of HeLa cells with polio virus type 1. VHH PVSP29F stabilized the poliovirus capsid against heat, preventing RNA release. Binding of VHH PVSP29F to the virus blocked attachment of polio virus type 1 to HeLa cells, in a concentration-dependent manner. Binding of VHH PVSP29F to the virus was shown to block the cell-induced conversion of 160S to 80S particles during infection. Neutralization of the virus was partially reversible by dilution of the VHH-poliovirus complex.

The poliovirus 1 Mahoney strain used to select the escape mutants contained substitution L228I in VP1.
